title: Cohort B Authorization Board
mission: Determine readiness for expansion beyond Cohort B. Consume S853/S854/S855 results and issue executive decision.

S853_Analyze.verdict: PASS — Quality-first pipeline detected and corrected its own defect

S854_Evaluate.gap_rationale: Only 2 of 12 Section F REMEDIATE items had genuine Evaluate potential. Forcing upgrades on definition-recall items would produce false cognitive labels.
S854_Evaluate.verdict: PASS — Quality over quantity. Classification integrity verified.

S855_Calibration.pipeline_gap_found: CognitiveLevel upgrades did not trigger Difficulty recalibration — systematic gap identified
S855_Calibration.verdict: PARTIAL_PASS — Critical items recalibrated. Pipeline gap documented for Cohort C.

Board_A-E_Content_Growth.note: Section E, the weakest readiness domain (0.5976), received 22 Analyze items. Section F received its first 3 Evaluate items.

Board_F-J_Quality.note: The self-introduced DL-008 on P1-EC-008 (EW_A/D slot transposition) was the critical quality signal: detected-immediately-corrected-immediately.

Board_K-O_Throughput.analyze_items_per_hour: ~4 (authoring batch) — limited by serial edit tool throughput
Board_K-O_Throughput.evaluate_items_per_hour: ~1 (requires full stem redesign for non-natural candidates)
Board_K-O_Throughput.key_limitation: Template-based authoring pipeline produced 83% definition-recall items in Section F. Genuine Evaluate potential existed in only ~17% of REMEDIATE candidates. Throughput is bounded by item quality, not tool speed.
Board_K-O_Throughput.note: Scaling Cohort C requires selecting candidates from sections with higher Evaluate potential (Sections C/D rather than Section F) or writing new items.

conditions: 1. Target Sections C (Performance Management) and D (Cost Management) for Evaluate candidates — these sections have higher Judgment/Analysis content than Section F definition-recall templates
2. Integrate Difficulty recalibration into the CognitiveLevel upgrade workflow — no separate calibration wave. Cross-validate Difficulty label when CognitiveLevel changes.
3. Address Pack C Section F structural corruption (15 unparseable items, 42 XXXMARKER artifacts) before Cohort C certification wave
4. Continue independent Classification Board review for every Evaluate upgrade — maintain 0% false-upgrade rate
5. Limit Cohort C scope to ≤50 items with at least 50% at Evaluate/Above levels
not_recommended: BROAD PILOT EXPANSION — premature. The pipeline has proven safety and quality but not scaled throughput. Content inventory (Analyze/Evaluate depth) is insufficient for broad learner deployment.
HOLD — unnecessary. The pipeline is functioning correctly under real authoring conditions.
Board_U-Z_Executive.rationale: The S853-S856 chain demonstrated that Framework v2 can safely create higher-order content at scale (22 Analyze in one session). The self-detected-and-corrected defect proves the quality-first pipeline works. However, throughput is limited by the template-based pool — only ~17% of Section F items have natural Evaluate potential. Cohort C should target richer sections (C/D) and integrate the calibration fix.

pipeline_maturity.scaled_throughput: NOT_YET_PROVEN — limited by template pool quality
pipeline_maturity.calibration_integration: NOT_YET — requires Cohort C workflow fix

strategic_outcome.readiness_score_impact: Marginal improvement in Section E/F (22 Analyze + 3 Evaluate). Primary readiness gains will come from Cohort C targeting Sections C/D.

revisionHistory.summary: Cohort B Authorization Board: AUTHORIZE COHORT C WITH CONDITIONS. Pipeline proven safe and quality-first. Throughput bounded by template pool quality. Cohort C to target Sections C/D with integrated calibration.
